title.bn: নাইভ বেইজ: শব্দ গুনে message-এর দল বাছা

summary.en: Count a tiny bilingual vocabulary, apply Laplace smoothing and compare class log scores before fitting a full SMS pipeline.
summary.bn: ছোট দ্বিভাষিক vocabulary-র শব্দ গুনো, Laplace smoothing করো এবং ক্লাস log score মেলিয়ে SMS predict করো।

sections.title: Separate message counts from word counts
Count, smooth and compare the same query
Change the words while preserving the model
Match the tiny counts before broadening vocabulary
What naive means and what tokenisation loses
Optional: Bayes comparison in log space
A small baseline with visible assumptions

examples.title: Count two word features and add log evidence
examples.explanationHtml: Only free and ক্লাস are features in this six-message demonstration. Class zero is ham and one is spam. Each class has four selected word occurrences, so smoothing adds one to each of two counts before dividing by six.

examples.title: Match the same two-feature scores with MultinomialNB
examples.explanationHtml: Whitespace tokenisation preserves the Bangla word as written. The fixed vocabulary matches the scratch counts exactly. Public learned log-prior and log-likelihood arrays reconstruct the joint scores; normalised predict_log_proba values would be different numbers.

examples.title: Learn a broader vocabulary from invented course SMS
examples.explanationHtml: The vectorizer learns its vocabulary only from training messages. These course messages are invented; a random-row score does not establish performance on future real messages or new campaigns. Whitespace tokenisation is an explicit simple policy, not full Bangla linguistic analysis.

practice.title: Classify a supplied two-feature message collection
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 2 to 10, then n lines starting with binary label and a space followed by text. Each text has at most 80 characters. Both classes must occur. Read a query line of at most 80 characters. Use only free and ক্লাস, lowercase whitespace tokens, alpha one and empirical class priors. Print prediction and both joint log scores to three decimals. Unknown words contribute nothing; ties choose zero. Invalid input prints invalid.
hints: Count documents for priors and words for likelihoods.
Smoothing changes the denominator by vocabulary size.

practice.title: Smooth a two-feature class count row
practice.statementHtml: Read two integer counts from 0 through 100. Add one to each and normalise by their original total plus two. Print both probabilities to three decimals. Invalid input prints invalid.
hints: The two resulting probabilities must sum to one before rounding.

practice.title: Explain the naive assumption
practice.statementHtml: Why can correlated words make naive Bayes too confident even when its chosen label is often useful?
hints: Distinguish useful decisions from calibrated confidence.
practice.answerHtml: The model multiplies feature evidence as if the features were conditionally independent given the class. Correlated words may repeat similar evidence, exaggerating confidence. The model can still be a useful baseline, but probabilities need evaluation rather than automatic trust.

practice.title: Audit an SMS split
practice.statementHtml: Why can near-duplicate campaign messages in both training and test inflate a reported score?
hints: Consider which similarities cross the split.
practice.answerHtml: A random split can place nearly identical templates on both sides, making the test less representative of new campaigns. Use a split aligned with future deployment, such as grouped templates or time when appropriate, and report the invented-data limits.

quiz.prompt: Read the table: which class receives stronger evidence from free free?
options: Neither class can score repeated words
quiz.explanation: Spam uses (5/6)² while ham uses (1/6)². Equal priors do not change their ordering.

caption.en: Smoothed likelihoods after counting six messages.
caption.bn: ছয়টি message গোনার পর smoothing করা likelihood দেখো।

quiz.prompt: Read the count row: with alpha one, what is P(free|ham)?
quiz.explanation: Add one to the zero count and two to the total four because the vocabulary has two entries.

caption.en: The raw selected-word counts for one class.
caption.bn: একটি ক্লাস-এর দুটি word ফিচার-এর raw count দেখো।

quiz.prompt: What does naive refer to in this model?
options: Conditional independence of features given the class
quiz.explanation: Real word features can be correlated, so the assumption is an approximation.

options: Avoid zero likelihood for an in-vocabulary word unseen in a class
quiz.explanation: The denominator must receive the corresponding vocabulary-size adjustment.

quiz.prompt: What happens to a word outside this fixed vocabulary?
options: It gets an arbitrary probability one
quiz.explanation: Unknown vocabulary and unseen-in-class words are different cases.

quiz.prompt: Why add log probabilities rather than multiply many tiny values directly?
options: To avoid numerical underflow while preserving score order
quiz.explanation: A sum of logs represents the product without repeated tiny multiplication.

quiz.prompt: Which data should fit the text vectorizer?
quiz.explanation: Vocabulary learning is a fitting step and belongs inside the training pipeline.

quiz.prompt: How many selected free occurrences are in this message?
quiz.explanation: The exact token free appears twice; ফ্রি is a different token outside the tiny vocabulary.

quiz.prompt: Which smoothed probability follows zero versus four selected counts?
quiz.explanation: The numerator becomes one and denominator six.

quiz.prompt: Which log score is larger for the label decision?
quiz.explanation: Minus 1.058 is the larger score, so class one wins.

keyPoints.en: Count documents for class priors and token occurrences for word likelihoods.
keyPoints.bn: ক্লাস prior-এর জন্য message গুনো, word likelihood-এর জন্য শব্দের occurrence গুনো।

keyPoints.en: The naive assumption treats feature evidence as conditionally independent.
keyPoints.bn: Naive ধারণায় ক্লাস জানা থাকলে ফিচার-এর প্রমাণগুলোকে স্বাধীন ধরা হয়।

keyPoints.en: Smoothing adjusts both a word count and the class total denominator.
keyPoints.bn: Smoothing-এ শব্দের count ও ক্লাস-এর মোট denominator দুটোই বদলায়।

keyPoints.en: Out-of-vocabulary words differ from known words unseen in one class.
keyPoints.bn: Vocabulary-র বাইরে শব্দ আর এক ক্লাস-এ না দেখা পরিচিত শব্দ আলাদা।

keyPoints.en: Joint log scores are not normalised posterior probabilities.
keyPoints.bn: Joint log score-কে স্বাভাবিক করা posterior probability ধরে নিও না।

examQuestions.question: Compute smoothed word likelihoods for class counts (4,0) with vocabulary size two and alpha one.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The total is four and the smoothed denominator is 4+2=6. The likelihoods are (4+1)/6=5/6 and (0+1)/6=1/6. They sum to one. Adding one only to a numerator without updating the denominator would not produce the stated model.

examQuestions.question: Compare joint scores for free free under the tiny equal-prior model.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Ham score is 0.5×(1/6)²=1/72≈0.013889, with log score −4.277. Spam score is 0.5×(5/6)²=25/72≈0.347222, with log score −1.058. Predict spam. Normalising gives spam posterior 25/26≈0.962; the joint score 0.347222 itself is not that posterior.

examQuestions.question: Explain one modelling assumption and one evaluation limitation for bilingual SMS.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Multinomial naive Bayes treats token evidence as conditionally independent given the class, so correlated phrases can exaggerate confidence. Whitespace tokenisation is an explicit simple representation and may miss language structure. A random split of invented or near-duplicate templates cannot establish future real-message performance; choose representative grouped or temporal evaluation as appropriate.
